newsitem.title: FINLAND: US OK FOR RAISIO'S BENECOL MAY TAKE A YEAR -PAPER.
newsitem.headline: US OK FOR RAISIO'S BENECOL MAY TAKE A YEAR -PAPER.

text.p: Finnish food group Raisio may have to wait a year for approval for its cholesterol-cutting agent Benecol from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, daily Helsingin Sanomat reported on Wednesday.
Raisio will need approval if it wants to market Benecol as being cholesterol-reducing, it said.

It quoted FDA spokesman Judy Foulke as saying the FDA would first investigate whether the application is justified, then make a proposal, and a final decision would take nine months. On top of that, two 90-day postponements were possible.
"Based on this, I think it would take a year," she said.
The paper said Raisio's U.S. partner McNeil, which is part of U.S. healthcare product giant Johnson & Johnson , had planned to start test marketing at the beginning of next year.
The key Benecol ingredient is stanol ester, which Raisio exclusively produces in fat-soluble form to make it useable as a food ingredient.
News last week of Raisio's partnership with McNeil to market the product in the U.S. boosted Raisio's share price by almost 70 percent.
